observation_kind: targeted current official polygon lifecycle, planning query, DSM service and Terrain 50 GML identity checks; not independent bulk HTTP fetches
rules: National Polygon index polygons are held in vector format.
Title plans and registers normally record the general position of boundaries unless an exact boundary has been determined.
Every registered title has at least one index polygon.
Each index polygon has a unique Poly_ID.
The title number manages the relationship between a registered title and its index polygons.
Index polygons are mapped against Ordnance Survey large-scale MasterMap data.
Ownership boundaries do not always follow features mapped in MasterMap.
The National Polygon Dataset is a subset of the Land Register containing all registered titles relating to land or property.
The National Polygon Dataset is closely linked to the Title Descriptor and UPRN datasets.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset with simpler identifier, creation-date and last-update attributes.
The mandatory Shape field stores single-area index-polygon geometry.
Poly_ID is mandatory and managed through dataset lifecycle rules.
Title_No is a mandatory character field identifying a registered title.
INSERT is a mandatory date recording initial polygon creation on the index map.
UPDATE is a mandatory date recording the last update to all or part of the title.
Vers_No is the mandatory version number of the Poly_ID.
Rec_Status identifies Added, Changed or Deleted polygon states.
The dataset contains genuine and erroneous overlaps, gaps, slivers and underlaps.
Overlaps below 0.5 square metres are not referred to caseworkers for remedial action.
HM Land Registry index polygons are captured in British National Grid.
The Planning Data API provides access to over 100 planning and housing datasets through one interface.
Latitude and longitude filters return entities whose geometry intersects the supplied point.
Multiple dataset parameters can be supplied and results may come from any selected dataset.
For registered properties, querying with a UPRN through q is more precise than a coordinate.
Entity responses include name, dataset, start-date, geometry WKT and point WKT among other fields.
An absence of results must not be presented as proof that no constraints exist because coverage varies.
The documentation shows all 337 local planning authorities can be fetched in one request.
geometry_entity can use an entity boundary for spatial filtering without pasting a raw polygon.
Listed-building entities include a listed_building_grade field.
The planning-application data specification is in development and may change.
Planning applications can be filtered with start-date components and a start-date match mode.
Custom geometry filters use WKT and spaces in WKT must be percent-encoded.
Custom-area coordinates are expected in WGS84, EPSG:4326.
Responses include next, previous, first and last pagination links.
The API has no batch endpoint, so portfolio screening requires one request per property or bulk local processing.
The 2m composite DSM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The 2m DSM is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
The DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain.
The 2022 DSM combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest best-resolution source is selected.
Bilinear interpolation is used when source data is resampled before merging.
The 2022 composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
The 2m DSM is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevation values are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15.
Individual input surveys have documented vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
The dataset has no public-access constraints and is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The metadata records an annual update frequency.
The dataset coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The official metadata identifier is f083c5dc-504f-4428-9811-a1b2519fa279.
The record exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS, survey-index and OGC API feature service surfaces.
OS Terrain 50 contour GML uses ContourLine, SpotHeight and LandWaterBoundary feature types.
ContourLine geometry is represented as GM_LineString.
Contour line types include master, ordinary and auxiliary.
SpotHeight geometry is represented as GM_Point.
Spot-height subtypes provide formSpot, generic, mountainPass and summit values.
LandWaterBoundary geometry is represented as GM_LineString.
Water-level categories include mean high/low water and Scottish mean high/low water springs.
Feature identifiers follow the os.t50.<tile>.<sequential-number> pattern.
Geometry identifiers use the feature identifier with a .geom suffix.
OS Terrain products are updated by whole-tile refresh rather than feature change-only updates.
The GML coordinate reference system is expressed as urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::27700.
A contour tile supply contains a tile GML data file and a Metadata_<tile>.xml file.
